clue.text: Fine words

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a punishment handed down by a court, as a verb or noun
second meaning: a grammatical unit made of a string of words

explanation.walkthrough: Fine looks like an adjective praising the words, but it is a penalty, read as the thing a judge passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes a sentence as a penalty, and a sentence is also a grammatical string of words.

clue.text: Fed up youngsters beginning to flout authority

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of youngsters

explanation.surface: Youngsters who are sick of being told what to do start rebelling against their elders.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to openly resist or disobey those in charge, a synonym for flouting authority.

clue.text: Blustery at first, with frequent showers, but bright

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of blustery
weather with frequent showers is wet weather

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: windy to begin with, then showery, but with sunny spells.
explanation.walkthrough: Bright looks like the forecaster's sunny spells, but here it means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of intelligent and quick-witted is a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Overweight actors playing the villains?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for fat people, the noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: big, burly people
second meaning: theatre slang for performers cast as the bad guys

explanation.surface: A casting director gives all the bad-guy parts to the larger members of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: Overweight reads as describing the actors, but it is a separate meaning: hefty, burly folk.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre and film slang the heavy is the villain's role, and burly people or hired thugs share the name.

clue.text: How to get your clothes aired and spotless?

parts.note: aired laundry has had the damp taken out of it
spotless means free of dirt
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: Household advice on getting your clothes freshened up and free of marks.
explanation.definitionFit: This process cleans garments using a chemical solvent rather than water, which is a way of treating your clothes.

clue.text: Out of danger, sailing past Holland

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for escaping trouble or blame
second meaning: offshore from the Hook of Holland, a Dutch port and ferry terminal

explanation.surface: A ship that has passed the Dutch coast is safe from the perils of the voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hook of Holland is a headland and ferry port on the Dutch coast, served by ferries from Harwich in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone freed from a difficulty or an obligation, as a fish slipping a line.

clue.text: Stay outside, or go

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps round the word that follows it

parts.note: to stay put is to rest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice put to someone: remain where you are, or leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is the only link; go is the definition, as in resorting to a place you visit often.
explanation.definitionFit: To resort to a place is to go there habitually, so the verb works as a synonym for go.

clue.text: Take part in a show trial

definitions.text: Take part in a show trial

parts.note: the surface reading: a staged political prosecution

parts.words: Take part in a show trial
parts.note: the setter's reading: play your part in a trial run of a stage show

explanation.surface: Someone is roped into a rigged political prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before a play opens, so actors doing it are trying the show out.

clue.text: Automatic umpire on Roman law

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
lex is the Latin word for law
joins the two pieces, umpire placed before law

explanation.surface: A referee instinctively applies the rules of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an involuntary, instinctive response, so as an adjective it means done without conscious thought.

clue.text: Tarry rope

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to linger or remain
second meaning: a rope bracing a ship's mast

explanation.surface: Rope coated in tar, as on an old sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarry looks like the adjective covered in tar; it is the verb meaning linger.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to remain somewhere, and on a sailing vessel a mast is braced by heavy lines with this name.

clue.text: A plea to be satisfyingly employed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prayer or appeal to a higher power

definitions.note: read as two words, in vocation
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: working at one's calling

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a job that is fulfilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after two letters: being in your calling is being happily employed.
explanation.definitionFit: An invocation is a prayer calling on a god for help, a solemn appeal or entreaty.

clue.text: Power drive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capacity to do work in physics
second meaning: vigour and enthusiasm in a person

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue sounds like a power drive on a tool; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists measure work in this quantity, and an energetic person is said to have plenty of vigour and get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Control said to be restored

parts.note: to rein in is to control, as with a horse
said and stated are synonyms

explanation.surface: An official announcement that order has been brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate someone or something is to put it back in its former position, which is to restore it.

clue.text: The rudiments of meteorology

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the basic principles of a subject

definitions.note: the elements is a name for the weather
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the weather, which meteorologists study

explanation.surface: An introductory course in weather science.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics of a subject are its first principles, and wind and rain together are often called the forces of nature.

clue.text: Instance of wickedness in a dull environment

definitions.text: Instance of wickedness in a dull environment

indicators.note: the whole clue doubles as a description of mischief
in says one word sits inside the surrounding word

parts.note: dull and boring is dry
wickedness is evil

explanation.surface: Mischief breaking out in a tedious setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Wickedness sits inside the dull word, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wicked or reckless mischief, so an act of it is an instance of wickedness.

clue.text: Exchange of gunfire's declining

definitions.note: read as re-fusing, fitting new fuses
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: replacing the fuses of guns
second meaning: saying no

explanation.surface: A shootout is dying down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as re-fusing, the word means fitting new fuses, a whimsical exchange of the fire in guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing an offer is turning it down, which is exactly what declining means.

clue.text: Bill fit to sing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statement of charges for goods supplied

definitions.note: read as two words, in voice
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: with the voice in good form

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man named Bill is well enough to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Split after two letters: a singer who is in voice is fit to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a document requesting payment for goods or services, a synonym for a bill.

clue.text: Reckon to make a hundred on the side, right?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cricketer wonders whether to score a century for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a hundred is cricket talk for a batsman scoring a century, which is what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon something is to regard or judge it to be so, a synonym of the verb meaning think.

clue.text: Term that's musical or legal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged in some other way

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a word belongs to music or to the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Legal looks like the second half of the definition, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is an Italian tempo marking meaning fast and lively, a word found in sheet music.

clue.text: Standard fails in production of Wagner opera

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: a production puts something together, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A staging of a Wagner opera falls below the usual standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Richard Wagner's final opera, about a knight of the Holy Grail.

clue.text: They fight with one another

parts.note: the surface reading: people quarrelling among themselves
the setter's reading: with means alongside, so they battle on the same side

explanation.surface: A description of people who keep scrapping among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are nations or people joined in a common cause, who go to war side by side.

clue.text: Jabbing a petty officer with a ruler

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for petty officer
a king is a ruler
joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A naval officer being prodded with a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruler suggests the measuring stick used for jabbing, but it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking someone is prodding them with a finger or stick, a synonym for jabbing.

clue.text: Father quick to get high religious office

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pacy means fast

explanation.surface: A priest rushes to win promotion in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office or position of the Pope, the highest post in the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Chars keen for a complete change

definitions.note: a cryptic description: cleaners eager to clean and sweep
definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptically: what cleaning women are eager to do, tidy and brush
second meaning: an idiom for removing everything old and starting afresh

explanation.surface: Cleaning ladies eager to give the place a thorough going-over.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is British for a woman paid to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a total removal of the old order, as when a new boss replaces all the staff.

clue.text: Eager to behead the king of Israel

indicators.note: to behead is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: David was the second king of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone keen to execute the Israelite monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid describes someone keenly enthusiastic, a direct synonym for eager.

clue.text: A number set up an alliance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised to read from the bottom

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: Several countries establish a pact.
explanation.walkthrough: The Axis was the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Axis is used for a coalition of states, most famously the wartime pact of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Humble cleric takes me in

indicators.note: takes in means the cleric word holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest churchman lets the speaker into his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Humble looks like an adjective describing the cleric; it is the verb meaning to lower.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, which is what humbling them does.

clue.text: Criminal set?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who handles stolen goods
second meaning: a radio or television set

explanation.walkthrough: Criminal set looks like a gang of crooks; split them into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence who deals in stolen property is a receiver, and a radio set that picks up signals has the same name.
